key: Shedding the ancient fluid he is poured into the cleansing sieve: He, thundering, hath produced the Gods.
s: The hymn opens with Soma engendering the sun and the lights of heaven, and follows the juice as it is purified; Sāyaṇa, on 9.42.4, reads his begetting the gods as figurative, since wherever Soma is pressed, there the gods invariably appear.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 9.42.4, Sanskrit Wikisource, revision 310169 (2021)

evidence.words: “क्रन्दन् शब्दं कुर्वन् "देवानजीजनत् जनयति स्वसमीपे । यत्र सोमोऽभिषूयते तत्र देवा नियतं प्रादुर्भवन्ति । अतो जनयतीत्युपचर्यते
evidence.gloss: ‘Crying out’: making a sound; ‘he generated the gods’: he generates them near himself. Wherever Soma is pressed, there the gods invariably become manifest; therefore ‘generates’ is said figuratively (upacāra).
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: day.js and verse.js confirm the key (ok true, ref 9.42.4, at [764,4]). Sāyaṇa on 9.42.4, in the packet source I opened, glosses ajījanat as janayati svasamīpe and explains that wherever Soma is pressed the gods invariably appear, so ‘generates’ is upacāra (figurative): the reading is his, at this place. Sāyaṇa on 9.42.1 has Soma generating the heavenly lights and the sun, so the opening clause holds. CHANGED the plain sense only: the proposal said the hymn ‘here turns to the straining of the juice’, but verses 2 and 3 already have Soma flowing purely and the juices purified, so it now reads ‘and follows the juice as it is purified’. src year 2021 confirmed by the MediaWiki API (revision 310169, 2021-05-14). Evidence is a contiguous span of the packet; entry-check ok.
